source.title: Avoiding Kernel Fixed Points: Computing with ELU and GELU Infinite Networks
source.authors: Russell Tsuchida; Tim Pearce; Christopher van der Heide; Fred Roosta; M. Gallagher

record.tranche_reason: The study measures training and test error across depth and activation functions in Gaussian-process regression, a different method and setting from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: No random-label fitting, interpolation-width sweep, classifier architecture comparison, optimizer or batch-size comparison, dropout experiment, magnitude-aware sharpness measurement, or memorized-example removal. Figures 8 and 11 report depth-dependent errors; only the Figure 8 sine-task results are extracted here.
record.test_reason: The study measures depth-dependent errors in infinite-width MLP Gaussian-process regression and analyzes kernel fixed points. These results do not test any listed version. Changing depth at infinite width does not test V2's widening beyond interpolation; the references to Zhang et al. and Neyshabur et al. provide motivation rather than replications.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the Figure 8 result. The broader conclusion is that GELU and ELU kernels can avoid the unique fixed points associated with ReLU's simplicity bias; kernel suitability depends on the task, with no consistently superior kernel. The authors acknowledge limitations of using infinite-width GPs to explain finite-network performance.
record.recipe_differences: Bayesian GP regression using infinite-width MLP covariance functions; the plotted depth experiment uses synthetic regression targets rather than standard gradient training on natural labels.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported depth trend differs by activation: GELU overfits with depth, while ReLU underfits.

fits_no_version.finding: On the noisy sine regression task, the authors report that increasing GP kernel depth produces overfitting with GELU and underfitting with ReLU.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-dependent kernel fixed-point behavior can produce different depth-dependent regularization effects in infinite-width MLP Gaussian-process regression.

record.problems: The extracted depth result is a figure without numeric values in the text and is based on a synthetic regression task and infinite-width GP covariance functions, not trained finite networks on natural labels.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 11 and 12 show additional target functions, but are omitted because the 60-row limit is not reached and Figure 8 provides the stated sine-task result. Other GP benchmark regression results do not report training-versus-test error gaps.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with generalization on natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning and recovery conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce them.
Dropout's effect on held-out classification error. Table 3 contains cited benchmark results, not an original dropout intervention.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The cannot_determine states concern applicability to V1–V8, not doubt about the authors' stated Figure 8 trends. Additional synthetic targets are declared in rows_left_out and do not test a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No random labels, memorization-capacity test, or natural-label classification.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected network comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: GP with iterated GELU covariance function
rows.operation_detail: Varied depth L from 1 to 100 and measured training and test MSE on the sine task.

conditions.value: x ∈ R2 uniformly sampled on the unit disc at heading γ

rows.measure: Training and test MSE as depth varies
rows.uncertainty: ± two standard deviations over 10 training data samples
rows.note: Authors describe GELU as overfitting with depth; no numeric values are stated in the text.
rows.check: The reported GELU overfitting trend is supported by the Figure 8 caption, but it cannot establish any listed version's effect. Training targets are sin(γ) plus Gaussian noise of variance 0.1, rather than noiseless sin(γ). Training and test MSE should be separate measure rows; numeric values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
